---
title: Writing with agents
description: What a glossary gives an AI agent, what the render checks, and what it does not.
---

## What it does and does not do

A [[controlled-vocabulary]] gives an agent built on an [[llm]] a plain list of
terms and their exact wording. The render stops on any `[[key]]` that is not in
the list, which catches mistyped and invented keys.

The render does not read plain prose. An agent that writes "decision point"
without brackets passes the render, even when the vocabulary says "decision
epoch". Whether an agent uses your terms depends on your instructions and your
review.

## Setup

1. Keep the vocabulary in the repository, in `glossary.yml` or in the
   document's [[front-matter]]. See [Ways to define terms](define-terms.qmd).
2. Leave [[strict-mode]] on. It is the default.
3. Tell the agent the rules in the instructions file it reads, such as
   `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
4. Make `quarto render` part of the agent's definition of done, and of CI.

## Instructions to copy

Replace `glossary.yml` with wherever your vocabulary lives: one or more
files, the `glossary.entries` of a document, or the front matter of included
fragments.

```markdown
## Vocabulary

- Use only the terms defined in glossary.yml. Refer to each one as [[id]],
  for example [[sample-size]]. Use [[id|plural]] for plurals and
  [[id|cap:plural]] at the start of a sentence.
- Do not paraphrase a defined term or invent a synonym for it, and do not
  use custom display text ([[id|other words]]) to introduce one.
- If a concept has no entry, stop and propose one with id, term, and
  definition. Do not add it to glossary.yml without approval.
- Keep definitions to one or two plain sentences. Put arguments and
  citations in the text.
- Before choosing a key, list the vocabulary the page can use:
  `quarto render <page> -M glossary-list:true 2>&1 | grep '^glossary entry'`.
- Run `quarto render` before you finish. Read the lines that start with
  `glossary:` or `glossary warning:` (`quarto render 2>&1 | grep '^glossary'`).
  One message lists every unknown key in a document, with the nearest
  existing key where there is one. Fix all of them before rendering again.
```

## What a failure looks like

When the agent writes keys that the vocabulary does not define, the render
stops and lists every one of them, with a suggestion where a defined key is
close:

```console
$ quarto render chapter-2.qmd
glossary: 2 problems:
  unknown glossary key [[robust-estimator]] in chapter-2.qmd:41
  unknown glossary key [[Sample-size]] in chapter-2.qmd:12, chapter-2.qmd:58; did you mean [[sample-size]]?
```

A key with two different definitions fails the same way and names both
places and the field that differs. Identical copies, such as a fragment
included twice, are accepted:

```console
glossary: glossary id 'se' is defined differently in glossary.yml and
glossary.entries (definition differs). Give one of them another id, or make
the two definitions identical
```

Either message is a prompt for a decision: add the entry, or rewrite the
sentence with an existing term.

## Reviewing new entries

Treat a proposed entry like a code change. Check that the wording matches your
field, that the definition is short enough for a balloon, and that the term
does not duplicate an existing one under another name. `see` and `see-also`
link related entries, and the render fails if either names an unknown key.

## Checking in CI

The repository's own workflow renders the documents on every push. Any
project can do the same with the Quarto GitHub action:

```yaml
- uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
- run: quarto render
```

A pull request with an undefined key then gets a red check before a person
reviews the text.
